title: Add escalation scenario simulator and compact sanity annotator
author: Maya Singh
description: Motivation: on-call teams need a lightweight way to validate that playbooks and escalation policies behave under realistic multi-service cascades without standing up heavy simulation infra. This PR introduces two complementary tools: (1) an escalation scenario simulator (CLI + scheduler) that can synthesize alert cascades, inject controlled flakiness, and exercise escalation paths; and (2) a compact sanity annotator that produces one-page annotated reports intended for pager handoffs and quick triage. The simulator supports pluggable probes, probabilistic failure models, and integrates with incident-bot to post simulated cards into test channels. The annotator collates traces/metrics/log snippets and applies heuristics to highlight likely root-cause signals and confidence scores so responders get a prioritized short checklist. What changed: new CLI under src/cli/escalation_sim, scheduler job manifests under infra/schedules, a small web-adapter for incident-bot integration under integrations/incident-bot-adapter, the annotator library under src/annotator with a compact JSON report format and human-readable rendering, docs updated with usage examples and a safety section, and unit+integration tests. Safety and rollout: all simulated runs default to a sandbox channel and a dry-run mode; incident-bot adapter requires an explicit test-token and a config flag to allow posting. The rollout plan is staged: enable nightly smoke runs for a small set of synthetic scenarios, validate with oncall rotation for two weeks, then expose the scenario authoring UI to SREs. Follow-ups: expand probe library, add RBAC for scenario execution, and wire results into the console metrics dashboard. Related: ENG-4921 for simulator design and SRE-88 for handoff UX improvements.
